answer.decision: Choose staged canaries with automatic abort thresholds and backward-compatible additive schema changes, but treat fast mitigation of database read-pattern failures as a release gate before broad rollout.
answer.action: Begin with a 1% canary held for at least 12 minutes, using automatic error-rate and p95-latency aborts. If healthy, promote through progressively larger regional stages and reach all traffic within one business day. On a routing regression, immediately disable the routing feature flag. On a database read-pattern regression, stop promotion and roll back the application while retaining additive schema fields. Do not promote to a stage where failures could drive customer error rate above 1% until database-path mitigation can restore compliance within five minutes or the constraint is explicitly revised.
reasons: Staged canaries minimize blast radius while providing statistically useful latency evidence.
Prior routing regressions became observable within four minutes, making automatic aborts appropriate.
The additive schema is safely compatible with the old application, so application rollback requires no schema downgrade.
Feature-flag disablement provides rapid mitigation for routing failures without redeployment.
A nine-minute application rollback cannot by itself guarantee the five-minute error-duration constraint for database read-pattern failures.
Global deployment creates excessive exposure, while production-identical staging would add six weeks without reproducing third-party latency variance.
assumptions: Traffic allocation can be controlled reliably by percentage and region.
Error rate and p95 latency can be evaluated and acted upon automatically in near real time.
The routing feature flag can be disabled within the five-minute limit.
Customer error rate is measured across the relevant customer population, so a 1% canary limits aggregate exposure during initial validation.
risks: The available evidence provides no fast disable mechanism for database read-pattern changes; broad rollout could therefore violate the five-minute constraint.
A 1% canary may miss region-specific or low-frequency failures.
The 12-minute initial hold reduces the time available for later stages but remains compatible with a one-business-day rollout.
Previously observed detection times do not guarantee that every new regression will be detected within four minutes.

citations.claim: The previous three routing regressions were detectable through error rate or p95 latency within four minutes.
The schema changes are additive and safely ignored by the old application version.
A 1% canary produces statistically useful latency signals in about 12 minutes.
Global application rollback takes nine minutes.
Production-identical staging would take six weeks and still would not reproduce third-party latency variance.
Routing can be disabled without redeployment, but database read-pattern changes require application rollback.
Customer error rate must not exceed 1% for more than five minutes.
Rollback must not require a schema downgrade.
A healthy rollout should reach all traffic within one business day.
